There are a few layers to this situation, including "What is the actual or 'most objective' color of the dress" and more abstract ones involving the phenomenon of difference in human perception. I think the photo is incredibly poor in terms of accurately depicting the 'real' colors. To me, looking at a true "black" border around the photo (#000000), it does not match very well to the "Black" parts of the dress. However, if you have a "white" border around the photo (#FFFFFF), it seems to more closely match the "Blue" parts of the dress. Turns out it can be attributed to super crappy white balance, so the photographer needs to get a better camera and/or editing software to produce a more accurate image with correct colorization.

Check this out: https://i.imgur.com/dIDJuQo.jpg

But really, I would argue the phenomenon surrounding the differences in perception -- not just the fact that people see different colors when looking at the exact same thing, but especially how people react to someone else having a different (yet equally strong) opinion from them, is the big takeaway here. Perception is not an automatically objective way to interpret something; everything experienced by a person is the result of sensory input and the brain's interpretation of it. We might be better off if more people began to understand that biases such as cognitive dissonance exist, and that peoples brains aren't nearly as infallible as most people believe they are.
